title: Describe a shipment with types
objective: Add a required priority to the shipment model and display it.
tasks: Add priority to Shipment as the union standard | express.
Give S-101 express priority and the other shipments standard priority.
Render the priority beside each shipment status; confirm all three rows remain visible.
hints: Start in /shipments.ts. A required field means every array entry needs a value.
Use shipment.priority inside JSX braces in /App.tsx.

title: Derive the manifest summary
objective: Calculate summary values from the typed records.
tasks: Calculate totalPallets with reduce and readyCount with filter from shipments.
Add a Summary section above the list showing the shipment count, pallet total, and ready count.
Confirm the supplied records show 3 shipments, 16 pallets, and 2 ready; change a record temporarily to check the summary follows.
hints: Use 0 as the initial reduce accumulator.
Derive counts during render rather than storing a second copy of the data.

title: Render the counter component
objective: Build a small semantic component before adding behavior.
tasks: Replace the placeholder paragraph with a short instruction about counting pallets.
Add a section labelled Pallet counter and render count inside an output element.
Give the output aria-live="polite"; confirm the preview shows Pallets: 0.
hints: Use className for CSS classes and braces to render a JavaScript value.
Keep the existing default App export and stylesheet import.

title: Remember the pallet count
objective: Use local React state to update the rendered count.
tasks: Import useState and replace the fixed count with useState(0).
Add an Add pallet button whose click handler increments with a functional state updater.
Click three times and confirm the displayed count becomes 3 without reloading.
hints: useState returns the current value and its setter.
Pass a function to onClick; call the setter inside it rather than during render.

title: Bound subtraction and reset
objective: Keep a nonnegative counter through every available action.
tasks: Add Remove pallet with a functional updater clamped to zero.
Disable Remove pallet at zero and add Reset that sets count to zero.
Check Add three times → Remove → Reset; repeat Remove at zero and verify the count stays zero.
hints: Math.max(0, current - 1) protects the update itself.
Reset sets the one source of truth; the output and disabled state derive from it.

title: Build the counter layout
objective: Render a reusable counter before introducing changing state.
tasks: Add a controls div containing five native buttons: -100, -1, Reset, +1, +100.
Keep the displayed value at zero and render Counter inside App.
Check that all five controls are visible and keyboard focus reaches them. They intentionally do nothing yet.
hints: Use className="controls" for the supplied layout.
Keep the value in an output element; changing values comes in the next lesson.

title: Make the counter interactive
objective: Use local React state to connect the five counter controls.
tasks: Import useState and initialize value to zero inside Counter; render value instead of the literal zero.
Wire ±1 and ±100 using functional updates so repeated clicks accumulate.
Make Reset set the value to zero. Try +100, -1, Reset, then -100.
hints: An event handler is a function: onClick={() => setValue(current => current + 1)}.
Reset replaces state; incrementing derives the next state from the previous value.

title: Create an observable counter store
objective: Move counter behavior into a class with observable state and bound actions.
tasks: In the constructor call makeAutoObservable(this, {}, { autoBind: true }).
Implement add as an accumulating action. Ignore non-finite deltas and results instead of storing NaN or Infinity.
Implement reset and verify the same five controls. Read why the supporting App still copies the store value into local state.
hints: Compute const next = this.value + delta, then use Number.isFinite on both delta and next.
autoBind keeps reset safe when passed directly as an event callback. makeAutoObservable does not subscribe a React component.

title: Subscribe React with observer
objective: Render observable values without a duplicate local-state snapshot.
tasks: Wrap Counter in observer from mobx-react-lite, keeping its counter prop.
Read counter.value during the observed render and leave actions on the store.
Check +100 then -1 displays 99, and Reset works without calling a React setter.
hints: Use const Counter = observer(function Counter(...) { return ...; });.
The starter changes the model on click but has no render subscription. Wrapping only App would not track reads inside the unwrapped Counter.

title: Manage multiple counters
objective: Compose observable counter instances in an observable parent collection.
tasks: Implement Store.addCounter: stop at safetyLimit, then push new CounterStore(this.nextId++).
Replace the single Counter with a map over store.counters and use counter.id as its React key.
Add several counters, change each independently, and confirm resetting one does not change the others.
hints: The supplied parent App is an observer because it reads the observable list. Each Counter is also an observer because it reads its own value.
IDs are assigned once and excluded from observation. The temporary safety limit of 20 prevents an unbounded teaching preview; the next step adds a four-counter business rule.

title: Derive capacity and the total
objective: Use computed getters for the four-counter limit and sum.
tasks: Derive canAddMoreCounters from counters.length and limit, then use it inside addCounter.
Derive sum with reduce over all counter values; do not store a separately maintained total.
Add up to four counters. Confirm Add counter becomes disabled and changing or resetting any counter updates the total.
hints: makeAutoObservable turns getters into computed values. Return this.counters.length < this.limit.
The disabled button is feedback; the guard in addCounter enforces the same rule for every caller.

title: Remove a counter safely
objective: Remove by stable identity while derived state updates automatically.
tasks: Implement removeCounter with filter, excluding the supplied ID and retaining the other instances.
Fill all four slots, assign different values, and remove a middle counter. Check the remaining IDs and values.
Verify capacity and total update, add a new counter, then remove all counters and recover using Add counter.
hints: Assign this.counters = this.counters.filter(counter => counter.id !== id).
Do not renumber survivors or reset nextId after removal; identity is separate from array position.

title: Restore and serialize URL state
objective: Hydrate validated values and synchronize them with the URL using a disposed reaction.
tasks: Implement serializedValues as a semicolon-separated value list and hydrate as an all-or-nothing validated replacement.
Reject more than four counters, payloads longer than 512 characters, blank tokens, NaN and Infinity. Treat an entirely empty string as an empty collection.
Implement restoreUrl and syncUrl. Use the value query parameter, preserve other parameters and the hash, catch browser failures, and return the reaction disposer.
Load 5;-2, change a value, and inspect the share query. Invalid input such as 1;;2 or Infinity must preserve the current collection. In the exported app, reload a URL containing ?value=5%3B-2.
hints: Validate all tokens first; only then map them to new CounterStore(this.nextId++, value) instances.
reaction(() => store.serializedValues, value => {...}, { fireImmediately: true }) returns a disposer. The supplied React effect returns it on unmount.
Use new URL(window.location.href), url.searchParams.set, and history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", url), inside try/catch.

title: Persist counters in localStorage
objective: Restore validated browser data and dispose both URL and storage synchronization.
tasks: Complete connectPersistence: a valid URL has priority, otherwise restore a validated JSON number array from STORAGE_KEY.
Catch storage access and JSON errors. Reject non-arrays, more than four items, oversized JSON, non-number values and non-finite numbers.
After restoration, use autorun to save only a plain array of counter values; catch quota or blocked-storage errors.
Return cleanup that stops both effects. Verify empty arrays, malformed JSON, URL priority and restoration after removing the value query parameter.
hints: JSON.parse returns untrusted data: assign it to unknown, then narrow with Array.isArray and an every check. Reuse store.hydrate only after validation.
autorun runs immediately. Restore first so a default snapshot cannot overwrite the saved values before they are read.
Keep storage and URL effects inside connectPersistence, called by the supplied useEffect. Return both disposers; do not start an autorun at module scope.

View state chooses a presentation. It should not replace the loading records.

title: Write the first store tests
objective: Turn behavior into assertions executed by Vitest in a terminal.
tasks: Replace the first two it.todo calls with executable tests using a new CounterStore in each test.
Assert the initial value is 0, then in the second test assert change(4) gives 4 and change(-2) gives 2.
Export your edited project and run pnpm exec vitest run in a real terminal; expect two passing tests and three pending.
hints: Store.change accepts a delta, not the desired final value.
The browser buttons call the real store, but they never execute /Store.test.ts.

title: Test both clamping boundaries
objective: Verify overshoots and repeated attempts at the limits.
tasks: Replace the clamping it.todo with a fresh-store test that changes by +100, +1, -100, then -1.
Assert values 10, 10, 0, and 0 after the respective operations.
Run the actual Vitest suite in a terminal; expect three passing tests and two pending.
hints: Large changes check clamping, while the additional ±1 checks the behavior at an already-reached boundary.
Keep the earlier tests intact so ordinary additions and subtraction remain covered.

title: Test reset and independent stores
objective: Prove reset changes a nonzero value and instances do not share state.
tasks: Replace the reset todo: change a new store by 7, assert 7, reset, then assert 0.
Replace the independence todo: create two stores, change only the first by 3, and assert first.value is 3 while second.value is 0.
Run Vitest in a terminal; expect all five tests passing with no pending cases.
hints: Resetting a store that is already zero would not detect a broken reset.
Construct the two independent stores inside the same test so their values can be compared.

title: Fetch the local ramp fixture
objective: Make a request and render its JSON response through the existing effect.
tasks: In loadRamps call fetch(url, { signal }), await the response, and return its parsed JSON as Ramp[].
Keep loadLocalRamps and /public/ramps.json unchanged; the adapter supports the preview and local Vite paths.
Confirm the preview moves from an empty result to the three named ramps.
hints: response.json() is asynchronous too.
The temporary Ramp[] assertion describes the expected shape; the next lesson will validate it at runtime.

title: Reject HTTP and invalid data
objective: Validate the response before treating it as ramp data.
tasks: Check response.ok before JSON parsing; throw an Error containing response.status for a failed HTTP response.
Parse JSON as unknown and require an array of objects with string id and name fields before returning Ramp[].
Toggle the missing fixture to inspect the error UI, then restore the working URL.
Temporarily change a fixture name to a number to exercise invalid data; restore the file afterwards.
hints: fetch can resolve on 404: a resolved promise is not the same as an OK HTTP status.
A Vite missing path may return HTML with status 200; the JSON parse error must still reach the error UI.

title: Cancel obsolete requests
objective: Pair every effect request with cancellation and stale-result protection.
tasks: Create an AbortController inside each effect setup and pass controller.signal to loadLocalRamps.
In cleanup set active to false before calling controller.abort().
Keep both success and error handlers guarded by active; rapidly toggle the missing-fixture option and check the final selection wins.
hints: Create the controller inside useEffect so each request gets its own signal.
The active guard ignores stale completions; abort stops unnecessary work. Keep both.

title: Retry the same request
objective: Start a fresh request without changing the URL or reloading the page.
tasks: Add a request counter with useState(0).
Enable Retry request and increment that counter with a functional update on each click.
Include request in the effect dependencies alongside url; retry success and failure, then restore the working fixture.
hints: Changing a dependency reruns the effect even when url is unchanged.
The existing effect resets loading and error and cleans up the previous request; use that same path for retry.

title: Add a UI5 provider and button
objective: Compose a UI5 React component inside its provider.
tasks: Import ThemeProvider and Button from their @ui5/webcomponents-react component paths.
Wrap the existing main element in ThemeProvider.
Replace the native button with Button, keeping its Load pallet text; confirm it renders and accepts keyboard focus.
hints: The lesson already includes matching UI5 v2 dependencies.
Place the provider inside App for this exercise; the generated entry does not add another one.

title: Wire actions and register icons
objective: Update React state from UI5 buttons with registered icons.
tasks: Add loaded state initialized to 0 and render it in the pallet count with aria-live="polite".
